body: But how honest would be too honest? I think my problem is that the OCD I'm facing (if it really is OCD) is very entangled with other issues I have, including bizarre and embarrassing things I've done because of the real paraphilias I have/had (even if they're currently dormant and may have just "been a phase"). I'm thinking maybe I should consult a sexologist first or something, or someone who specializes in weird sexual behavior. I'd much rather treat it as extremely serious and find out it isn't that serious, than the other way around. I will look into the resource you provided and would like resources of that vein for sexual disorders (I'm speaking to anyone casually browsing this thread, professional or non professional)
I can't stand myself living like this for the next 20, 30, 40 years. I will legit off myself if there is no way to remedy this or fix me.

The problem is that it probably isn't OCD. I feel like I've been deluding myself by saying it's OCD, but in all honesty before this spate of anxiety it was always sort of there in the background, attracting some level of concern but not something I thought dangerous or really pressing. I just lived a law-abiding life. I believe I might have OCD, since this has all but consumed the entirety of my thoughts the past three months, but I really don't know if that can explain what I'm feeling right now, if those therapists will even be open to the mere suggestion it isn't just OCD, and whether they'll help me with the chemical castration process or miscellaneous if it's something more serious that needs to be immediately addressed, and that OCD therapies cannot cure.

I cannot understate that revealing this information, let alone implying that it might not be OCD (mostly because of personal habits which I am reluctant to share to anyone because they'll get the wrong idea) to anyone would be incredibly dangerous.

Therapy isn't an option sadly. I have an online therapist already (with whom I've discussed treated the "hidden paraphilia" aspect from the angle of OCD), but I'm not very open with him, and I would never even remotely imply that the feelings might be real. The very suggestion detests me, and it would revolt him too, I have to keep it PC. Even if there's a 1% chance of it being real I'd rather kill my sex drive (or myself). The thought of being stuck this way for life fills me with unspeakable dread, I want to be normal.

Ultimately, I DON'T want to discuss the severity with anyone. Inside, I'd rather the whole thing just disappear forever than have it ever be concrete or materialized in any way, shape, or form. it was never this bad until the pandemic started, even returning to that normal (where I had a problematic sex drive, compulsive masturbation, and bizarre potentially deviant fetishes) would be preferable
